content:
According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple is preparing multiple new features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 that will be more appealing to health-focused users. The company is also testing two finishes for a rumored ceramic version.

New health features upgrade

If you're dissatisfied with the current state of the Apple Watch as a fitness tracker, the following two key health feature upgrades should be quite appealing. The two features are all-day heart rate tracking and a redesigned app that makes it easier to extract useful insights from your health data. Here's Gurman's description of the new app:

As a current WHOOP user, I've always felt its biggest draw is that the WHOOP app makes it easier for me to learn from my health data. It shows me all the factors affecting my sleep or recovery, while the Apple Watch seems to only care about activity rings. If Apple makes meaningful progress here, I'll be quite happy.

To deliver a richer data experience on the Apple Watch, the key is having more data. Apple is reportedly testing the ability of its heart rate sensor to record throughout the entire day, rather than only during workouts or at random intervals.

Two new finishes

We've previously learned that Apple is considering a ceramic material for the Apple Watch Series 12, and Gurman now reports that it will be offered in two color options: a traditional white, and a dark gray. There will also be "multiple new color and combination options for bands."

A redesign on the horizon

The current Apple Watch design language, introduced in 2024 with the Apple Watch Series 12, was a relatively modest change, with the company slimming down the watch by narrowing the bezels. According to Bloomberg, we may see an all-new Apple Watch design next year, to coincide with the Series 13, or possibly pushed back to the Series 14:

I'm quite looking forward to seeing what Apple comes up with. The rounded design language seems to be reaching its limits, so perhaps we'll see an entirely new form factor. Hopefully it won't break backward compatibility with older bands.
